name: Telegram
description: Run Harvis from Telegram DMs, groups, and topics.

env_vars.description: Complete Telegram bot token created by @BotFather (numeric bot ID followed by a colon and secret)
Optional comma-separated numeric Telegram user IDs allowed immediately; leave blank to approve new users through DM pairing

name: Discord
description: Connect Harvis to Discord DMs, channels, and threads.

env_vars.description: Discord bot token from Developer Portal
Comma-separated Discord user IDs allowed to use the bot

name: Slack
description: Use Harvis from Slack via Socket Mode. Add allowed Slack member IDs so connected bots can respond.

env_vars.description: Slack bot token (xoxb-). Get from OAuth & Permissions after installing your app. Required scopes: chat:write, app_mentions:read, channels:history, groups:history, im:history, im:read, im:write, mpim:history, mpim:read, users:read, files:read, files:write
env_vars.help: In your Slack app, add the required bot scopes, install the app to the workspace, then copy OAuth & Permissions > Bot User OAuth Token.

env_vars.description: Slack app-level token (xapp-) for Socket Mode. Get from Basic Information → App-Level Tokens. Also ensure Event Subscriptions include: message.im, message.channels, message.groups, message.mpim, app_mention
env_vars.help: In your Slack app, enable Socket Mode, then create Basic Information > App-Level Tokens with the connections:write scope.

env_vars.description: Comma-separated Slack member IDs allowed to use Harvis, e.g. U01ABC2DEF3. Without this, Slack may connect but deny messages by default.
env_vars.help: In Slack, open your profile, choose More or the three-dot menu, then Copy member ID. Add multiple IDs comma-separated.

Matrix recovery key for cross-signing verification after device key rotation (from Element: Settings → Security → Recovery Key)

name: API server
description: Expose Harvis as an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API for tools like Open WebUI.

env_vars.description: Enable the OpenAI-compatible API server (true/false). Allows frontends like Open WebUI, LobeChat, etc. to connect.
Bearer token for API server authentication. Required whenever the API server is enabled; server refuses to start without it.
Port for the API server (default: 8642).
Host/bind address for the API server (default: 127.0.0.1). API_SERVER_KEY is still required even on loopback binds.
Model name advertised on /v1/models. Defaults to the profile name (or 'hermes-agent' for the default profile). Useful for multi-user setups with OpenWebUI.

name: Webhooks
description: Receive events from GitHub, GitLab, and other webhook sources.

env_vars.description: Enable the webhook platform adapter for receiving events from GitHub, GitLab, etc.
Port for the webhook HTTP server (default: 8644).
Global HMAC secret for webhook signature validation (overridable per route in config.yaml).

name: A2A
description: No extra packages needed (stdlib only)

env_vars.description: Name advertised on this agent's Agent Card (default: hostname-derived).
Shared bearer token for inbound A2A calls (identity falls back to caller IP). With no token of any kind => bind to 127.0.0.1 only (no remote access).
env_vars.prompt: A2A shared bearer token (or empty for localhost-only)

env_vars.description: Inbound bind host. Defaults to 127.0.0.1; only widens to 0.0.0.0 when a bearer token is set AND you opt in here.
Per-peer bearer tokens ('alice:tok1,bob:tok2'). Each remote agent gets its own credential; the matched name is the authenticated identity used for rate limiting, trust, and audit.
env_vars.prompt: A2A per-peer tokens (name:token, comma-separated; or empty)

env_vars.description: Inbound A2A server port (default 9900).

name: Buzz
description: Requires the buzz CLI binary (https://github.com/block/buzz) on PATH or at BUZZ_CLI_PATH

env_vars.description: Base URL of the Buzz community relay (e.g. https://mycommunity.communities.buzz.xyz)
Nostr private key for the agent's Buzz identity (nsec or hex) — the only Buzz secret
Comma-separated npubs or hex pubkeys allowed to talk to the agent
Optional NIP-OA owner-attestation auth tag JSON for NIP-42 WebSocket auth
Comma-separated channel UUIDs to watch (default: all joined channels)
Path to the buzz CLI binary (default: 'buzz' on PATH, then ~/bin/buzz)
JSON credentials file holding the nsec (fallback when BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY is unset)
Seconds between inbound poll sweeps (default: 4)
Thread replies under the triggering message (true/false, default: true); false posts flat to the channel timeline
Inbound transport: auto (WebSocket w/ poll fallback, default), websocket, or poll

name: iMessage via Photon
description: Use Harvis through iMessage via Photon's managed Spectrum platform.

env_vars.description: Spectrum project id (the project's spectrumProjectId; set by `hermes photon setup`)
Project secret paired with the Spectrum project id (set by `hermes photon setup`)
Comma-separated E.164 phone numbers allowed to talk to the bot
Photon Dashboard API host (default https://app.photon.codes)
Send agent replies as markdown — iMessage renders it natively, other Spectrum platforms degrade to plain text (true/false, default true)
Mention wake-word regexes for group chats (JSON list or comma/newline-separated; defaults to Harvis wake words)
Path to the node binary (default: shutil.which('node'))
Tapback 👀/👍/👎 on messages as processing status and route tapbacks on bot messages to the agent (true/false, default false)
Mark inbound iMessages read after forwarding to Harvis (true/false, default true)
Spawn the Node sidecar on connect (true/false, default true)
Loopback port for the Node sidecar control + inbound channel (default 8789)
Photon Spectrum API host (default https://spectrum.photon.codes)
Enable Spectrum SDK telemetry in the sidecar (true/false, default false; toggle with `hermes photon telemetry on|off`)
